model_annotation: This horizontal bar chart illustrates the number of participants who selected each of seven criteria when evaluating or rating something—likely a system, interface, or explanation—based on their perceived importance or relevance. The vertical axis lists the criteria in descending order of participant count: “Relevant FCs” (6 participants), “FC Summary” (5), “Relevance Explanation” (3), “Clarity and Simplicity” (3), “Overall Summary” (2), “Filters” (1), and “Veracity Explanation” (1). The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of Participants,” ranges from 0 to 6 with tick marks at intervals of 2. Each bar is color-coded and corresponds to a specific criterion, with bar lengths proportional to the number of participants. The longest bar, “Relevant FCs,” is dark purple, followed by “FC Summary” in medium purple, “Relevance Explanation” and “Clarity and Simplicity” in teal shades, “Overall Summary” in green, and “Filters” and “Veracity Explanation” in lighter green tones. The chart visually emphasizes that “Relevant FCs” was the most frequently selected criterion, while “Filters” and “Veracity Explanation” were selected by only one participant each.
